name: Cormac Brick
bio: Principal Engineer at Google working on edge AI.  Lead on the Google AI Edge team and contributes to Gemma Model development.  An early pioneer in Edge AI, his industry background includes leading Intel’s first laptop NPUs, as well as demonstrating edge AI on a USB key way back in NeurIPS 2016.  These days he is technical lead for a team that drives multiple open source projects (Google AI Edge Gallery, LiteRT-LM, LiterRT, Xnnpack, Mediapipe) that enable Edge AI for billions of users.

positions.claim: Reaching the majority of devices with AI requires models in the 50M–500M parameter range, not the 1–4B 'small model' class.
DRAM cost, not compute, is the binding constraint on edge AI deployment, and it is getting worse rather than better.
The low end of the LLM parameter spectrum is under-researched relative to large models.
A tiny fine-tuned model can match or exceed the quality of a 2–4B model on a single fixed task such as summarization or proofreading.
10,000 to 10 million synthetic samples is sufficient to fine-tune a tiny model to high reliability for a given task.
For small models the right playbook is zero-shot prompting and LoRA adapters, whereas for tiny models you must fine-tune unless an off-the-shelf fixed-task model exists.
Speedups from shrinking models come primarily from reading fewer bytes from memory per token, not from arithmetic reduction.
A 2B-class model needs roughly 4GB+ of device DRAM in practice once KV cache, runtime, and the OS are accounted for.
Raspberry Pi-class hardware running a 2B model is too slow to meet real-time user interaction requirements, while Jetson-class hardware is not.
Voice-to-function-calling is the key interaction pattern for edge and IoT devices because their settings-menu interfaces are hard for many people to use.
Generalizing voice-to-function-calling — ideally by having an agent generate the synthetic dataset for you — is the most important next step for tiny models.
Developing edge AI for first-party Google products first and then open-sourcing the tooling is the more effective route to broad adoption.
